title: Unknown-cause handling on valid TypeID 104 test command
purpose: Target the same general parser family implicated by the supplied issue using a valid TypeID 104 I-frame, but keep object count and body length consistent while setting an unusual cause to cover unsupported-cause branches safely.
expected_behavior: Implementation should parse a complete Test Command ASDU for TypeID 104, then reject, log, or classify it as unknown/unsupported because of the nonstandard cause value, without reading past the end of the message.
constraints_preserved: TypeID 104 is selected directly from the supplied GHSA issue description.
APCI length 0x0e is consistent with a single-object TypeID 104 ASDU of 10 bytes after the control field.
VSQ/object count is 1 and the message includes one full 3-octet information object address plus one command octet, maintaining internal size consistency.
Control field uses a simple I-frame sequence pattern with N(S)=1 and N(R)=0 encoded conservatively from IEC 60870-5-104 prior knowledge.

Cause value 0x2c is used as an unusual/unknown-style code by conservative assumption; the supplied sources indicate unknown-cause handling as a target concept but do not define this exact byte mapping.
issue_safety_notes: This is a structural analogue to the documented bug path because it uses TypeID 104, but it deliberately avoids the vulnerable shape: no inflated VSQ, no body truncation, and no copied PoC bytes.
